title: Go-live checklist
sub: Everything for real orders in two groups: what is needed before go-live (only these hold back the switch of the main domain) and what the owner does soon after go-live. Automatic items come from the server; the others are checked by a person and confirmed here.

safe.title: Only a list.
safe.text: Nothing here switches anything on or off, and the main domain is never switched from here. The backups have their own checks:

readOnly: You can see the list. Confirming an item needs the "Go-live" permission.

smoke.title: Every page opens (smoke test)
smoke.how: The smoke test after every deploy and every night must pass, and be recent: {failed} page(s) failed or it has not run lately (the Server page has the list).
smoke.why: Needed: a page that does not open loses real orders.

health.title: The server's health check is clean
health.how: The server's own check reports {problems} problem(s), or has not run lately; the Server page says which.
health.why: Needed: a sick server can stop orders or lose them.

backups.title: Last night's backup on the server
backups.ok: last night's server copy is good
backups.how: Last night's copy on the server did not go well, or is missing ({todo} to do) — open Settings → System → Backups and press "Back up now".
backups.why: Needed: with last night's copy on the server, a mistake can be undone.

offServer.title: Off-server backup (Azure Blob and Google Drive)
offServer.ok: Blob and Drive connected, each with a fresh copy
offServer.how: Off-server backup: not connected ({todo} check(s) to do). Connect Azure Blob and Google Drive in Settings → System → Backups; the yellow line on the Dashboard comes back every day until then.
offServer.why: Soon after: the server's own copy and its provider's snapshot keep the data meanwhile; the owner connects Blob and Drive from the admin.

restoreDrill.title: Restore drill of the off-server copies
restoreDrill.ok: the Blob and the Drive copy were brought back
restoreDrill.how: The monthly restore drill brings the Azure Blob and the Google Drive copy back into a throw-away database ({todo} still to do). It starts once both are connected; press "Run the restore drill now" in Settings → System → Backups.
restoreDrill.why: Soon after: it needs the off-server copies first; the server's own copy is tested every night meanwhile.

originCert.title: Cloudflare Origin certificate on the server
originCert.how: Make an Origin certificate in Cloudflare (SSL/TLS → Origin Server → Create certificate, for the main domain and *. of it) and paste the certificate and its private key into Keys & connections → Cloudflare origin certificate. Now: {error}. Main domains not covered: {missing}.
originCert.why: Needed: without it customers see a security error.

sslStrict.title: Cloudflare SSL/TLS mode is Full (strict)
sslStrict.how: Once the line above is done: Cloudflare → SSL/TLS → Overview → Full (strict), for the staging and the main domain. Open the shop afterwards; an error 526 means the certificate does not fit — set it back to Full and check the line above.
sslStrict.why: Needed: it keeps the line between Cloudflare and the server private.

ownerData.title: Store details and legal numbers (owner data)
ownerData.how: Owner data: to fill in — {missing}. The owner types them in Settings → Store details for each store (contact, address, legal numbers …; the list is the setting golive.ownerData) and his delivery charge in Delivery. Until then an empty detail is simply not shown on the shop.
ownerData.why: Soon after: the owner types his own details in the admin after go-live; an empty one is never shown to a customer.

connections.title: Live payment, courier and SMS keys
connections.how: In Keys & connections, enter each provider's keys and press Save and test; a passing test moves it from practice to live. Still on practice: {missing} (the list is the setting golive.connections). Until then: cash on delivery works without a key, and without an SMS key the customer gets no SMS.
connections.why: Soon after: a connection without its key stays on its mock, which is allowed at go-live.

telegram.title: Telegram connected
telegram.how: Keys & connections → Telegram: the bot's token and the chat, press Test. Then a failed night, the daily off-server backup line and the first-week check reach the owner's phone.
telegram.why: Soon after: meanwhile every alert is kept in the server's alert log and on the Server page.

indexing.title: Main domain open to search engines
indexing.how: On go-live day, after the switch: Website → SEO → let search engines in. It only counts on a store's main domain (Settings → Stores); the staging site always stays out. Main domains now: {hosts}.
indexing.why: Needed: on go-live day the new shop must be found on Google.

searchConsole.title: Search Console on the main domain, sitemap sent
searchConsole.how: In Google Search Console: the main domain's property is verified (a DNS record in Cloudflare is the simplest), /sitemap.xml is submitted under Sitemaps, and the old shop's property is kept to watch the move (PR 587). Then confirm.
searchConsole.why: Needed: Google learns the new pages and the old addresses move with them.

testPayments.title: Test payments off, every online method on a real gateway
testPayments.ok: off on every live store; every online method is real
testPayments.how: Money → Payments → switch "Test payment buttons" off on every store that goes live (still on: {stores}). Every wallet, card or online method offered must have its real gateway live in Keys & connections, or be switched off in the checkout's payment settings (still on practice: {methods}).
testPayments.why: Needed: nobody may mark an order paid without paying.

rateLimit.title: Request limits enforce
rateLimit.how: Settings → Security → Request limits: set the mode to "enforce" (now: {mode}), so sign-in guessing and fake orders are slowed down. Raise the per-minute numbers there first if many customers share one mobile address.
rateLimit.why: Needed: slows down password guessing and fake orders.

staffTwoFactor.title: Two-step sign-in for every staff member who can change things
staffTwoFactor.ok: every such staff member signs in with two steps
staffTwoFactor.how: {without} active staff member(s) who can change something have no two-step sign-in yet. Each turns it on for their own sign-in, or the owner requires it of everybody (Settings → Security → "Everyone must use two-step sign-in"; now: {required}).
staffTwoFactor.why: Needed: a stolen staff password alone cannot change the shop.

runbook.title: Go-live runbook read, rollback rehearsed
runbook.how: Read docs/golive/RUNBOOK.md (the switch minute by minute, and how each step is undone). On staging, run the Deploy workflow once with "Go back to the previous version" and once without, and note how long it took. Then confirm.
runbook.why: Needed: if the switch goes wrong, it can be undone in minutes.

qaGate.title: QA gate green (Blueprint Appendix C)
qaGate.how: The device gate at 0 failures on phones, tablets and desktop, the journeys and the Lighthouse budget pass in CI for the build on staging; the screenshots were looked at.
qaGate.why: Needed: every page works on phones, tablets and desktops.

erpAcceptance.title: ERP acceptance green against the demo ERP, with writes
erpAcceptance.ok: Stores on the v6 ERP: {stores} (none: not needed). Last demo run with writes: {passed} checks passed.
erpAcceptance.how: Stores on the v6 ERP: {stores}. The nightly ERP acceptance run against the demo ERP must pass every check with writes on (the setting "Let the acceptance check write to the demo ERP", `erp.acceptance.demoWrites`, switched on only once agreed with the ERP team) within the smoke test's hours. Last run: {state}, {passed} passed, {failed} failed, writes {writes}. See docs/reports/erp-acceptance/latest.
erpAcceptance.why: Needed when a store uses the v6 ERP: the shop and the ERP agree on orders, stock and the books before real orders.

acceptance.title: Staging acceptance list walked through
acceptance.how: Every line of docs/golive/ACCEPTANCE.md checked on the staging site as a customer and as admin.
acceptance.why: Needed: what a customer and the admin do was checked on staging.
acceptance.runOk: Last automatic run (acceptance workflow): passed, {at} — {passed} of {total} parts. Walk the person's lines of the list, then confirm.
acceptance.runFail: Last automatic run (acceptance workflow): not passed, {at} — {passed} of {total} parts passed. See docs/reports/acceptance/latest.
acceptance.runNone: No automatic run yet: GitHub › Actions › acceptance (by hand) runs the smoke test, the journeys, the test orders and the customer 360°.

realPhones.title: Real iPhone and real Android
realPhones.how: The shop opened and one order placed on a real iPhone (Safari) and a real Android phone (Chrome).
realPhones.why: Needed: real customers use real phones.

simulation.title: The real-life journey simulation passed on staging
simulation.how: The 70-order simulation of docs/qa/SIMULATION-PLAN.md rerun on the staging site, every finding fixed (CN-013).
simulation.why: Needed: the money and the orders add up across 70 real-life orders.
simulation.runOk: Last automatic run (simulation workflow): passed, {at} — {passed} passed, {failed} failed, {skipped} skipped of {planned} orders. Read its report, then confirm.
simulation.runFail: Last automatic run (simulation workflow): not passed, {at} — {failed} failed, {passed} passed, {skipped} skipped of {planned} orders. See docs/reports/simulation/latest.
simulation.runNone: No automatic run yet: GitHub › Actions › simulation (by hand) places the 70 orders on the mocks.

server.title: Every server item of A2.9 in place
server.how: The last full server setup run must pass every step (Blueprint A2.9.16): {fail} failed ({failed}). Run the "Server setup" workflow again after the fix; the report is in docs/reports/server/latest.md.
server.why: Needed: the server's own set-up protects the shop and its data.

securityReview.title: Outside security review
securityReview.how: The independent outside review (docs/security/REVIEW.md) is skipped by the owner. The automatic parts keep running: dependency scanning in CI on every build and every night, and the security checks. If a review is done later, confirm it here.
securityReview.why: Soon after: skipped by the owner; the automatic security checks run on every build.

firstWeek.title: First-week watch
firstWeek.sub: After the switch: for {days} days a daily check on Telegram at {time}, and the smoke test of every page every {hours} hours.
firstWeek.offText: Start it on go-live day, right after the switch.
firstWeek.lastText: The last watch ran from {from} until {until}.

golive.INVALID_INPUT: Not an item that can be confirmed here.

errors.FORBIDDEN: You do not have the permission for this.
errors.server-error: Something went wrong on the server; try again in a moment.
errors.network: The server cannot be reached — check the connection and try again.

before.title: Needed before go-live
before.sub: Only these hold back the switch of the main domain.

after.title: Soon after go-live
after.sub: The owner does these from the admin once the shop is live; they never hold back the switch and stay yellow until done.
